1→# Auto-Claude Configuration for Adamastor
     2→
     3→This file provides instructions for Auto-Claude agents working on Adamastor issues.
     4→
     5→## Critical Rules
     6→
     7→1. **Branch from staging** - All branches MUST be created from `staging`, never from `main`
     8→2. **PRs target staging** - All pull requests MUST target `staging`, never `main`
     9→3. **Regression tests required** - Every bug fix MUST include an E2E regression test
    10→4. **Reply to all PR comments** - Never leave review comments without responses
    11→5. **Wait for CI** - Do not request review until all CI checks are green
    12→
    13→## Complete Workflow
    14→
    15→### 1. Branch Creation
    16→```bash
    17→git checkout staging
    18→git pull origin staging
    19→git checkout -b <type>/issue-<number>-<short-description>
    20→```
    21→- Types: `fix/`, `feat/`, `refactor/`, `docs/`, `chore/`
    22→- Example: `fix/issue-42-district-filter`
    23→
    24→### 2. Issue Comment
    25→Post a comment on the issue stating:
    26→- What you're working on
    27→- Your planned approach
    28→- Any questions or clarifications
    29→
    30→### 3. Implementation
    31→- Read relevant files
    32→- Reproduce the problem (for bugs)
    33→- Implement the fix or feature
    34→- Run tests: `bun run test`
    35→
    36→### 4. E2E Regression Test (Bug Fixes Only)
    37→**MANDATORY** for all bug fixes. Add test to appropriate spec file in `apps/web/e2e/`:
    38→- `home.spec.ts` - Homepage bugs
    39→- `navigation.spec.ts` - Navigation bugs
    40→- `leaderboard.spec.ts` - Ranking page bugs
    41→- `postal-codes.spec.ts` - Postal code bugs
    42→- `parties.spec.ts` - Party page bugs
    43→
    44→Pattern:
    45→```typescript
    46→// Issue #XX: Brief title
    47→// @see https://github.com/bcamarneiro/adamastor/issues/XX
    48→test('descriptive test name', async ({ page }) => {
    49→  // Test the specific user flow that was broken
    50→});
    51→```
    52→
    53→Test locally: `cd apps/web && npx playwright test <spec-file>`
    54→
    55→### 5. Commit
    56→Format: `<type>(<scope>): <description> (#<issue-number>)`
    57→- Example: `fix(web): resolve district filter 400 error (#42)`
    58→- Types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
    59→
    60→### 6. Create PR
    61→```bash
    62→git push -u origin <branch-name>
    63→gh pr create --base staging --title "..." --body "Closes #<number>
    64→
    65→## What
    66→[Brief description]
    67→
    68→## Why
    69→[Why this change is needed]
    70→
    71→## How
    72→[Implementation details]
    73→
    74→## Testing
    75→- [ ] Unit tests pass
    76→- [ ] E2E tests pass (for bug fixes)
    77→- [ ] Manual testing completed
    78→"
    79→```
    80→
    81→**CRITICAL**: Use `--base staging`, NOT `--base main`.
    82→
    83→### 7. Wait for CI and Check for Copilot Comments
    84→
    85→#### Step 7a: Wait for CI to complete
    86→
    87→```bash
    88→gh run watch <run-id>
    89→```
    90→
    91→- All checks must pass: lint, typecheck, test-watcher, test-web, e2e, build
    92→- If CI fails, fix and push again
    93→
    94→#### Step 7b: Check for GitHub Copilot review comments
    95→
    96→**CRITICAL**: Before marking as ready for human review, check if Copilot already left comments:
    97→
    98→```bash
    99→# Check for any review comments
   100→gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments --jq '.reviews[], .comments[]'
   101→```
   102→
   103→If Copilot (or any automated reviewer) left comments:
   104→
   105→1. Address ALL comments following step 8 below
   106→2. Push fixes
   107→3. Wait for CI to pass again
   108→4. Verify all comments have replies
   109→5. Only then mark as ready for human review
   110→
   111→**Never send a PR to human review with:**
   112→
   113→- ❌ Failing CI checks
   114→- ❌ Unaddressed Copilot comments
   115→- ❌ Review comments without replies
   116→
   117→### 8. Address PR Review Comments
   118→If the PR receives review comments (from Copilot or humans):
   119→
   120→1. Check for comments:
   121→   ```bash
   122→   gh pr view <number> --comments
   123→   ```
   124→
   125→2. For each comment:
   126→   - Make the fix if appropriate
   127→   - Reply individually:
   128→     ```bash
   129→     gh api repos/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pulls/comments/<comment-id>/replies \
   130→       -f body="Fixed in commit <sha>. <description>"
   131→     ```
   132→   - OR explain why not changing:
   133→     ```bash
   134→     gh api repos/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pulls/comments/<comment-id>/replies \
   135→       -f body="Won't fix: <reasoning>"
   136→     ```
   137→
   138→3. After addressing all comments:
   139→   - Push fixes
   140→   - Wait for CI to pass
   141→   - Re-request review:
   142→     ```bash
   143→     gh pr edit <number> --add-reviewer @bcamarneiro
   144→     ```
   145→
   146→**CRITICAL**: Every comment must receive a reply.
   147→
   148→## Project Context
   149→
   150→**What is Adamastor?**
   151→Portuguese Parliament transparency platform tracking deputy attendance and performance.
   152→
   153→**Tech Stack:**
   154→- Monorepo with Turborepo
   155→- Bun (watcher), Vite (web)
   156→- TypeScript (strict mode)
   157→- Testing: Bun test (watcher), Vitest + Playwright E2E (web)
   158→- Database: Supabase (PostgreSQL)
   159→- UI: React + Radix UI + Tailwind CSS
   160→- Linting: Biome (not ESLint/Prettier)
   161→
   162→**Key Files:**
   163→- `apps/watcher/src/transform/` - Data pipeline (CRITICAL: affects data accuracy)
   164→- `apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` - E2E regression tests
   165→- `packages/shared/src/types.ts` - Shared TypeScript types
   166→- `supabase/migrations/*.sql` - Database migrations
   167→
   168→**Portuguese Context:**
   169→- **Legislatura** - Legislative term (currently XVII/17th)
   170→- **Deputado** - Deputy/MP
   171→- **Distrito** - Electoral district (22 total)
   172→- **Partido** - Political party (PS, PSD, CH, IL, BE, etc.)
   173→
   174→## Common Pitfalls to Avoid
   175→
   176→❌ Branching from `main` instead of `staging`
   177→❌ Creating PRs to `main` instead of `staging`
   178→❌ Forgetting E2E regression tests for bug fixes
   179→❌ Leaving PR review comments without replies
   180→❌ Requesting review before CI passes
   181→❌ Using `any` types in TypeScript
   182→❌ Modifying existing database migrations (create new ones)
   183→❌ Committing secrets or API keys
   184→
   185→## Testing Commands
   186→
   187→```bash
   188→# Root level
   189→bun install          # Install all dependencies
   190→bun lint             # Lint all packages (Biome)
   191→bun typecheck        # Type check all packages
   192→
   193→# App-specific
   194→bun --filter watcher test    # Run watcher unit tests
   195→bun --filter web test        # Run web unit tests
   196→bun --filter web build       # Build web app
   197→
   198→# E2E tests
   199→cd apps/web && npx playwright test
   200→cd apps/web && npx playwright test home.spec.ts  # Run specific spec
   201→```
   202→
   203→## Additional Resources
   204→
   205→- Full AI guidelines: `docs/AI_AGENTS.md`
   206→- GitHub Copilot context: `.github/copilot-instructions.md`
   207→- Architecture: `ARCHITECTURE.md`
   208→- Contributing: `CONTRIBUTING.md`

1→# Specification: Auto-Claude PR Creation Before Human Review
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Currently, when using auto-claude, the workflow completes by staging changes to the main project and marking the task as "human_review" - requiring the user to manually commit and create a PR. The user wants the workflow to automatically create a Pull Request after QA approval, so that human review happens in GitHub where CI status is visible. This eliminates manual terminal operations and enables validation through GitHub's PR interface.
     6→
     7→## Workflow Type
     8→
     9→**Type**: feature
    10→
    11→**Rationale**: This is an enhancement to the existing auto-claude workflow. It adds a new step (PR creation) between QA approval and human review, integrating with GitHub's PR and CI infrastructure. The core functionality exists; this extends it to provide a better developer experience.
    12→
    13→## Task Scope
    14→
    15→### Services Involved
    16→- **auto-claude MCP server** (primary) - The external MCP server that orchestrates the auto-build workflow
    17→- **git/GitHub CLI** (integration) - For branch pushing and PR creation via `gh pr create`
    18→
    19→### This Task Will:
    20→- [ ] Add automatic PR creation step after QA approval
    21→- [ ] Push worktree branch to remote before creating PR
    22→- [ ] Create PR using `gh pr create --base staging` with proper body format
    23→- [ ] Store PR URL in `implementation_plan.json`
    24→- [ ] Move task to "human_review" status only AFTER PR is created
    25→- [ ] Update `.auto-claude-status` to include PR URL for visibility
    26→
    27→### Out of Scope:
    28→- Modifying the actual code generation/implementation phases
    29→- Changing the QA approval process
    30→- Automatic merging of PRs
    31→- CI pipeline modifications
    32→
    33→## Service Context
    34→
    35→### Auto-Claude MCP Server
    36→
    37→**Tech Stack:**
    38→- Language: JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js)
    39→- Protocol: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
    40→- Key directories: External to this repository (provided as MCP server)
    41→
    42→**Entry Point:** MCP server runs as a subprocess providing tools
    43→
    44→**Available Tools:**
    45→```
    46→mcp__auto-claude__update_subtask_status
    47→mcp__auto-claude__get_build_progress
    48→mcp__auto-claude__record_discovery
    49→mcp__auto-claude__record_gotcha
    50→mcp__auto-claude__get_session_context
    51→mcp__auto-claude__update_qa_status
    52→```
    53→
    54→**How to Run:** Automatically started by Claude Code as MCP server
    55→
    56→### Adamastor Project (Target)
    57→
    58→**Tech Stack:**
    59→- Language: TypeScript
    60→- Framework: React (frontend), Bun (watcher)
    61→- Key directories:
    62→  - `.auto-claude/specs/` - Spec directories for each task
    63→  - `.worktrees/` - Git worktrees for parallel development
    64→
    65→**Entry Point:** N/A (repository being operated on)
    66→
    67→**How to Run:**
    68→```bash
    69→cd apps/web && npm run dev
    70→```
    71→
    72→**Port:** 3000 (web frontend)
    73→
    74→## Files to Modify
    75→
    76→| File | Service | What to Change |
    77→|------|---------|---------------|
    78→| MCP Server - workflow state machine | auto-claude | Add new state between "qa_approved" and "human_review" for PR creation |
    79→| MCP Server - PR creation logic | auto-claude | Implement `gh pr create` invocation after QA approval |
    80→| `implementation_plan.json` schema | auto-claude | Add `pr_url`, `pr_number`, `branch_pushed` fields |
    81→| `.auto-claude-status` schema | auto-claude | Add `pr_url` field for task visibility |
    82→
    83→## Files to Reference
    84→
    85→These files show patterns to follow:
    86→
    87→| File | Pattern to Copy |
    88→|------|----------------|
    89→| `.auto-claude/specs/*/implementation_plan.json` | Current schema structure with `status`, `qa_signoff`, `stagedAt` fields |
    90→| `AUTO_CLAUDE.md` | PR creation commands and body format for Adamastor |
    91→| `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Complete GitHub workflow including `gh pr create` patterns |
    92→
    93→## Patterns to Follow
    94→
    95→### PR Creation Pattern
    96→
    97→From `AUTO_CLAUDE.md`:
    98→
    99→```bash
   100→git push -u origin <branch-name>
   101→gh pr create --base staging --title "..." --body "Closes #<number>
   102→
   103→## What
   104→[Brief description]
   105→
   106→## Why
   107→[Why this change is needed]
   108→
   109→## How
   110→[Implementation details]
   111→
   112→## Testing
   113→- [ ] Unit tests pass
   114→- [ ] E2E tests pass (for bug fixes)
   115→- [ ] Manual testing completed
   116→"
   117→```
   118→
   119→**Key Points:**
   120→- Always use `--base staging`, never `main`
   121→- Include "Closes #<issue-number>" if linked to an issue
   122→- Structured body with What/Why/How/Testing sections
   123→
   124→### Implementation Plan Schema Pattern
   125→
   126→From `.auto-claude/specs/006-implement-loading-screen-component/implementation_plan.json`:
   127→
   128→```json
   129→{
   130→  "qa_signoff": {
   131→    "status": "approved",
   132→    "timestamp": "2026-01-07T18:35:00.000Z"
   133→  },
   134→  "status": "human_review",
   135→  "stagedAt": "2026-01-07T22:27:55.518Z",
   136→  "stagedInMainProject": true
   137→}
   138→```
   139→
   140→**Proposed New Fields:**
   141→```json
   142→{
   143→  "pr_created": {
   144→    "url": "https://github.com/bcamarneiro/adamastor/pull/123",
   145→    "number": 123,
   146→    "branch": "feat/spec-006-loading-screen",
   147→    "created_at": "2026-01-07T22:28:00.000Z"
   148→  },
   149→  "status": "human_review"
   150→}
   151→```
   152→
   153→## Requirements
   154→
   155→### Functional Requirements
   156→
   157→1. **Automatic PR Creation After QA Approval**
   158→   - Description: When QA agent approves a task, the workflow should automatically create a GitHub PR
   159→   - Acceptance: PR appears in GitHub repository after QA approval, before status changes to "human_review"
   160→
   161→2. **Branch Push Before PR**
   162→   - Description: Worktree branch must be pushed to remote before PR creation
   163→   - Acceptance: `git push -u origin <branch>` succeeds without manual intervention
   164→
   165→3. **PR URL Tracking**
   166→   - Description: The PR URL must be recorded in `implementation_plan.json`
   167→   - Acceptance: `pr_created.url` field contains valid GitHub PR URL
   168→
   169→4. **Human Review Triggered by PR**
   170→   - Description: Status changes to "human_review" only after PR is successfully created
   171→   - Acceptance: `status: "human_review"` only appears in implementation_plan.json when `pr_created.url` is set
   172→
   173→5. **CI Status Visibility**
   174→   - Description: User can validate changes in GitHub UI where CI status is displayed
   175→   - Acceptance: PR page shows CI checks running/passed/failed
   176→
   177→### Edge Cases
   178→
   179→1. **Branch Push Failure** - Retry push, or mark task as "push_failed" with error message for manual intervention
   180→2. **PR Creation Failure** - Retry with exponential backoff, or mark task as "pr_creation_failed" with error details
   181→3. **Duplicate PR Exists** - Check for existing PR on branch before creating new one; link to existing if found
   182→4. **No GitHub CLI Auth** - Fail gracefully with clear error message about `gh auth login` requirement
   183→5. **Remote Branch Already Exists** - Use `git push --force-with-lease` for safety
   184→
   185→## Implementation Notes
   186→
   187→### DO
   188→- Follow the PR body format in `AUTO_CLAUDE.md` exactly
   189→- Use `gh pr create` with `--base staging` always
   190→- Store PR URL immediately after creation for tracking
   191→- Check for existing PRs before creating duplicates
   192→- Use meaningful PR titles derived from spec/task name
   193→
   194→### DON'T
   195→- Create PRs targeting `main` branch
   196→- Skip the branch push step (PR creation will fail)
   197→- Leave tasks in "human_review" without a PR URL
   198→- Use `git push --force` (prefer `--force-with-lease`)
   199→- Create PRs without running QA approval first
   200→
   201→## Development Environment
   202→
   203→### Start Services
   204→
   205→```bash
   206→# Auto-claude MCP server starts automatically with Claude Code
   207→# For Adamastor development:
   208→cd apps/web && npm run dev
   209→```
   210→
   211→### Service URLs
   212→- Web Frontend: http://localhost:3000
   213→- Supabase (local): http://127.0.0.1:54321
   214→
   215→### Required Environment Variables
   216→- `GITHUB_TOKEN`: GitHub CLI authentication (handled by `gh auth login`)
   217→- `SUPABASE_URL`: Database connection (existing)
   218→- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`: Database auth (existing)
   219→
   220→## Success Criteria
   221→
   222→The task is complete when:
   223→
   224→1. [ ] After QA approval, a PR is automatically created targeting `staging` branch
   225→2. [ ] PR URL is stored in `implementation_plan.json` under `pr_created.url`
   226→3. [ ] Task status becomes "human_review" only after PR creation succeeds
   227→4. [ ] User can click PR URL to view changes in GitHub
   228→5. [ ] CI checks are visible on the PR page
   229→6. [ ] No manual terminal commands required between QA approval and human review
   230→7. [ ] Existing tests still pass
   231→8. [ ] No console errors during workflow execution
   232→
   233→## QA Acceptance Criteria
   234→
   235→**CRITICAL**: These criteria must be verified by the QA Agent before sign-off.
   236→
   237→### Unit Tests
   238→| Test | File | What to Verify |
   239→|------|------|----------------|
   240→| PR creation command | MCP server test file | `gh pr create` called with correct args |
   241→| Branch push logic | MCP server test file | `git push -u origin` called before PR creation |
   242→| Status transition | MCP server test file | Status only changes to "human_review" after PR URL set |
   243→| Duplicate PR check | MCP server test file | Existing PR detection works correctly |

"""
Execution phase event protocol for frontend synchronization.

Protocol: __EXEC_PHASE__:{"phase":"coding","message":"Starting"}
"""

import json
import os
import sys
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any

PHASE_MARKER_PREFIX = "__EXEC_PHASE__:"
_DEBUG = os.environ.get("DEBUG", "").lower() in ("1", "true", "yes")


class ExecutionPhase(str, Enum):
    """Maps to frontend's ExecutionPhase type for task card badges."""

    PLANNING = "planning"
    CODING = "coding"
    QA_REVIEW = "qa_review"
    QA_FIXING = "qa_fixing"
    COMPLETE = "complete"
    FAILED = "failed"


def emit_phase(
    phase: ExecutionPhase | str,
    message: str = "",
    *,
    progress: int | None = None,
    subtask: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Emit structured phase event to stdout for frontend parsing."""
    phase_value = phase.value if isinstance(phase, ExecutionPhase) else phase

    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
        "phase": phase_value,
        "message": message,
    }

    if progress is not None:
        if not (0 <= progress <= 100):
            progress = max(0, min(100, progress))
        payload["progress"] = progress

    if subtask is not None:
        payload["subtask"] = subtask

    try:
        print(f"{PHASE_MARKER_PREFIX}{json.dumps(payload, default=str)}", flush=True)
    except (OSError, UnicodeEncodeError) as e:
        if _DEBUG:
            print(f"[phase_event] emit failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)

   114→    def update_status_from_subtasks(self):
   115→        """Update overall status and planStatus based on subtask completion state.
   116→
   117→        This syncs the task status with the UI's expected values:
   118→        - status: backlog, in_progress, ai_review, human_review, done
   119→        - planStatus: pending, in_progress, review, completed
   120→
   121→        Note: Preserves human_review/review status when it represents plan approval stage
   122→        (all subtasks pending but user needs to approve the plan before coding starts).
   123→        """
   124→        all_subtasks = [s for p in self.phases for s in p.subtasks]
   125→
   126→        if not all_subtasks:
   127→            # No subtasks yet - stay in backlog/pending
   128→            if not self.status:
   129→                self.status = "backlog"
   130→            if not self.planStatus:
   131→                self.planStatus = "pending"
   132→            return
   133→
   134→        completed_count = sum(

   136→        )
   137→        failed_count = sum(1 for s in all_subtasks if s.status == SubtaskStatus.FAILED)
   138→        in_progress_count = sum(

   140→        )
   141→        total_count = len(all_subtasks)
   142→
   143→        # Determine status based on subtask states
   144→        if completed_count == total_count:
   145→            # All subtasks completed - check if QA approved
   146→            if self.qa_signoff and self.qa_signoff.get("status") == "approved":
   147→                self.status = "human_review"
   148→                self.planStatus = "review"
   149→            else:

   152→                self.planStatus = "review"
   153→        elif failed_count > 0:

   155→            self.status = "in_progress"
   156→            self.planStatus = "in_progress"
   157→        elif in_progress_count > 0 or completed_count > 0:

   160→            self.planStatus = "in_progress"
   161→        else:

   165→            if self.status == "human_review" and self.planStatus == "review":

    91→    """
    92→    Detect file renames between two git refs using git's rename detection.
    93→
    94→    This analyzes the commit history between two refs to find all file
    95→    renames/moves. Critical for merging changes from older branches that
    96→    used a different directory structure.
    97→
    98→    Uses git's -M flag for rename detection with high similarity threshold.
    99→
   100→    Args:
   101→        project_dir: Project directory
   102→        from_ref: Starting ref (e.g., merge-base commit or old branch)
   103→        to_ref: Target ref (e.g., current branch HEAD)
   104→
   105→    Returns:
   106→        Dict mapping old_path -> new_path for all renamed files
   107→    """
   108→    renames: dict[str, str] = {}
   109→
   110→    try:
   111→        # Use git log with rename detection to find all renames between refs
   112→        # -M flag enables rename detection
   113→        # --diff-filter=R shows only renames
   114→        # --name-status shows status and file names
   115→        result = subprocess.run(
   116→            [
   117→                "git",
   118→                "log",
   119→                "--name-status",
   120→                "-M",
   121→                "--diff-filter=R",
   122→                "--format=",  # No commit info, just file changes
   123→                f"{from_ref}..{to_ref}",
   124→            ],
   125→            cwd=project_dir,
   126→            capture_output=True,
   127→            text=True,
   128→        )
   129→
   130→        if result.returncode == 0:
   131→            for line in result.stdout.strip().split("\n"):
   132→                if line.startswith("R"):
   133→                    # Format: R100\told_path\tnew_path (tab-separated)
   134→                    parts = line.split("\t")
   135→                    if len(parts) >= 3:
   136→                        old_path = parts[1]
   137→                        new_path = parts[2]
   138→                        renames[old_path] = new_path

   166→        if worktrees_idx != -1:
